Compensation and allowance after the 2019 amendment

ItemCompensation (insured unemployed)Allowance (first-time job seeker)
Amount60% of the 12-month average wage200 for graduates, 150 for others
LimitsBHD 200 to 1,000—
Duration9 months, and 9 in every 24 months9 months within 12 months
Contributions required12 consecutive months for a first claimNone
NationalityBahrainis and legally resident expatriatesBahrainis only

Examples:
Average BHD 1,200: 720 × 9 = BHD 6,480.
Average 2,500: 60% = 1,500, capped at 1,000: 1,000 × 9 = BHD 9,000.
Average 300: 60% = 180, raised to the minimum: 200 × 9 = BHD 1,800.
Someone dismissed after only 8 months of contributions gets no compensation, but the allowance if Bahraini.

A second claim needs 12 months of contributions within 18, a third 18 within 24, and later claims 36 within 48. The right lapses if a suitable job is refused twice without good reason. For your end-of-service award, use the Bahrain end-of-service calculator.

Frequently asked questions

How much is unemployment compensation in Bahrain?

60% of the insured person's average wage over the previous 12 months, at least BHD 200 (or the average wage if lower) and at most BHD 1,000 a month, for up to 9 months, continuous or not (Articles 11, 12 and 14 as amended in 2019).

How much is the allowance for first-time job seekers in Bahrain?

BHD 200 a month for university graduates and 150 for others, for up to 9 months within 12 months, for Bahrainis aged 18 or over (Articles 17 and 18). Parliament approved raising it to 300 and 250 in 2025, but the amendment had not been issued by November 2026.

Do people who resign get unemployment compensation?

No. The worker must not have left the job voluntarily or been dismissed for disciplinary reasons (Article 10).

Can expatriates get unemployment compensation in Bahrain?

Yes for compensation, if legally resident and meeting the other conditions; the allowance is for Bahrainis only.

How much is the unemployment insurance contribution?

1% of the wage from the insured person, 1% from the employer (paid by the Labour Fund for the private sector) and 1% from the government (Article 6).

When does compensation start?

From the eighth day after employment ends if you register within 30 days, otherwise from the registration date; the right lapses if you do not register within 3 months (Articles 13 and 21).
